what: WORKED COMPUTATION (independent run 2 of 2): Newton's law between two records, in the linear model. Take the Gaussian field on the periodic L^3 lattice with covariance C = sigma^2/(1 - phi^2), phi = 1 - E(k)/7 (zero mode removed), the stationary equal-time law of linear light-cone formation. Condition on theta(x_1) = a and theta(x_2) = b. (1) Show the log-probability of the pair of pins is -(1/2) v^T K^-1 v with v = (a, b) and K the 2x2 matrix [[C(0), C(r)], [C(r), C(0)]]; expand the interaction part: -a b C(r)/(C(0)^2 - C(r)^2) ~ -a b C(r)/C(0)^2. (2) With C(r) ~ c/r this is a 1/r attraction between like pins: compute c exactly (7 sigma^2/(8 pi)) and tabulate the exact interaction for r = 1..L/2 along three directions at L = 32, 64, 128 by FFT, against c/r with the finite-size image correction. (3) Do the same for the backward lattice, phi = (1 + sum_j e^{ik_j})/4 (anisotropic metric M): give the equipotential surfaces. Expectation: 1/r within a few percent for 3 <= r <= L/6.
